8 sample questions, worked out

Straight from the test, with the answer and the reasoning shown. The full test gives you 120 of these, drawn fresh each time.

  1. Question 1 What is the most frequently used piece of sewer cleaning equipment?

    1. A. The bucket machine
    2. B. The cable machine
    3. C. A high-velocity jet cleaner Correct answer
    4. D. Hand rodding equipment

    Why High-velocity jet cleaners are truck- or trailer-mounted and self-contained, making them the most frequently used sewer-maintenance equipment: the most flexible option and the one that uses the least personnel.

    Source US EPA / NEIWPCC, Optimizing O&M and Rehabilitation of Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems (December 2003); high-velocity jet cleaners are the most frequently used sewer-maintenance equipment, the most flexible, and use the least personnel.

    Cleaning cctv equipment · Easy · Recall

  2. Question 2 Which type of pump is the standard choice for handling raw wastewater with solids, rags, and stringy debris without clogging?

    1. A. A standard end-suction centrifugal pump with an open impeller built for clean water
    2. B. A non-clog pump with an impeller designed to pass solids and rags Correct answer
    3. C. A positive-displacement piston pump built for high-pressure clean water service
    4. D. A jet pump built for shallow well suction lift

    Why Non-clog pumps use an impeller shaped to pass solids and stringy material without binding, which is why they are the standard choice for raw wastewater in lift stations. Matching the pump to the wastewater quality is a basic reliability rule; the wrong impeller design is the most common cause of a lift station pump that repeatedly clogs.

    Source US EPA, Collection Systems Technology Fact Sheet: Sewers, Lift Station (EPA 832-F-00-073); reliability improves by using non-clog pumps suited to the particular wastewater quality.

    Pump types · Easy · Recall

  3. Question 3 A 12-inch sewer (1.0 ft diameter) flows full at 1.57 cubic feet per second (cfs). What is the velocity of flow?

    1. A. 0.01 ft/s
    2. B. 1.57 ft/s
    3. C. 2.0 ft/s Correct answer
    4. D. 4.0 ft/s

    Why Velocity equals flow divided by area, and area equals 0.785 times diameter squared: 0.785 times 1.0 squared is 0.785 square feet, and 1.57 divided by 0.785 is 2.0 feet per second.

    Formula V = Q / A, A = 0.785 x D^2

    Pipe hydraulics · Medium · Application

  4. Question 4 Under a permit-required confined-space program, what is the acceptable oxygen range for entry?

    1. A. 25.0 percent to 30.0 percent
    2. B. 5.0 percent to 12.0 percent
    3. C. 19.5 percent to 23.5 percent Correct answer
    4. D. 10.0 percent to 15.0 percent

    Why Permit-required atmosphere limits set an acceptable oxygen entry level of 19.5 percent to 23.5 percent; normal breathing air is 20.9 percent oxygen, and the space must never fall below 19.5 percent.

    Source OSHA Permit-Required Confined Spaces standard, 29 CFR 1910.146, as reflected on the entry permit form; acceptable oxygen entry level is 19.5 percent to 23.5 percent.

    Confined space · Medium · Recall

  5. Question 5 How long should MIS (management information system) records for a collection-system maintenance program typically be kept?

    1. A. At least three years Correct answer
    2. B. At least three months
    3. C. Only for the current fiscal quarter
    4. D. No retention guideline exists

    Why MIS records should be kept at least three years, which supports the same 'if it's not recorded, it didn't happen' discipline applied to water-main break records.

    Source US EPA, Guide for Evaluating CMOM Programs at Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems (EPA 305-B-05-002, January 2005); MIS records should be kept at least three years.

    Recordkeeping · Easy · Recall

  6. Question 6 What does jetting do that flushing does not?

    1. A. Jetting only applies to storm sewers, never to sanitary sewers
    2. B. Jetting adds chemical root retardant to the water stream
    3. C. Jetting drives high-velocity water to remove debris and cut roots Correct answer
    4. D. Jetting requires the line to be completely dry before starting

    Why Flushing introduces a heavy flow of water at a manhole to move lighter deposits; jetting goes further, directing high-velocity water against the pipe walls to remove heavier debris and grease and to cut roots in small-diameter pipe.

    Source US EPA / NEIWPCC, Optimizing O&M and Rehabilitation of Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems (December 2003); jetting drives high-velocity water against the walls to remove heavier debris, grease, and clogs, and cuts roots in small-diameter pipe.

    Rodders and jetters · Medium · Recall

  7. Question 7 What are the four basic elements of a force main?

    1. A. Wet well, dry well, screen, and grinder
    2. B. Manhole, invert, bench, and channel
    3. C. Basin, weir, baffle, and launder
    4. D. Pipe, valves, surge control, cleaning system Correct answer

    Why A force main's four elements are pipe, valves, pressure-surge control devices, and a cleaning system; it is the pressurized pipe that carries wastewater from the discharge side of a pump to a discharge point.

    Source US EPA, Wastewater Technology Fact Sheet: Sewers, Force Main (EPA 832-F-00-071); a force main's four elements are pipe, valves, pressure-surge control devices, and a cleaning system.

    Valves · Medium · Recall

  8. Question 8 A rectangular wet well is 6 feet by 5 feet, with water standing 4 feet deep. How many gallons does that represent?

    1. A. About 120 gallons
    2. B. About 224 gallons
    3. C. About 1,795 gallons
    4. D. About 898 gallons Correct answer

    Why Wet-well volume in gallons equals length times width times depth, times 7.48 gallons per cubic foot: 6 times 5 times 4 is 120 cubic feet, times 7.48 is about 898 gallons.

    Formula Wet-well volume (gal) = L x W x Depth (ft) x 7.48

    Wet wells · Medium · Application
